gap.title: Part 2 of 2 of a proof of: Conjecture: circuits of AND and OR gates for the edge function of a graph with no cycle shorter than 5 have size linear in the number
gap.formal_statement: ∃ (x1 : ℕ), ∀ (x2 : ℕ) (x3 : SimpleGraph (Fin x2)) [x4 : DecidableRel x3.Adj], (∀ (x5 : Fin x2) (x6 : x3.Walk x5 x5), x6.IsCycle → (5 : ℕ) ≤ x6.length) → x3.edgeFinset.Nonempty → ∀ (x7 : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit), PEqualNP.TopForm.IsLeastAO x3 x7 → PEqualNP.TopForm.TopForm x3 x7 → (PEqualNP.TopForm.Ustar x3 x7).card ≤ x1 * (x7.size + (1 : ℕ))
gap.plain_statement: One of 2 statements that together prove: There is a constant c such that for every graph G with no cycle of length below 5, and every circuit of AND and OR gates only, each reading at most two wires, every gate counted, that is true exactly when both ends of some edge of G are true, the number of edges of G is at most c times (the number of gates + 1). The constant is fixed before the graph. It carries content only on dense graphs, such as point-line incidence graphs of projective planes. Conjecture.
